S1.1.2 Unit4 ERP Implementation Overview MQI currently use Exchequer Enterprise for its financial software. This system has been in place for many years. However, Exchequer no longer meets the needs of the organisation. We have decided to migrate our financial systems to Unit4 ERP. MQI is procuring implementation services, post go-live hypercare and ongoing application support services in relation to the Unit4 ERP solution. Tenderers should note that core Unit4 SaaS platform support, product support, incident management, service availability management and access to the Unit4 support organisation remain the responsibility of Unit4 under the relevant Unit4 subscription and support arrangements. The services sought under this procurement are intended to complement, rather than replace, the support services provided directly by Unit4 and are focused on implementation delivery, application support, configuration assistance, user support, optimisation and advisory services. INTRODUCTION 1.1 The Merchants Quay Ireland ("MQI") invites tenders ("Tenders") in response to this Request for Tenders ("RFT") from economic operators ("Tenderers") for the provision of the services as described in Schedule 1 to this RFT (the "Services"). 1.2 MQI is a national charity and one of Ireland’s largest providers of homelessness, addiction, and social inclusion services, supporting thousands of people each year through a national network of services. MQI is a company limited by guarantee and a registered charity, governed by a voluntary Board of Directors and subject to the Charities Regulator, the Charities Governance Code, and applicable funder and statutory oversight requirements. MQI delivers contracted and grant-funded services in partnership with the Health Service Executive, the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage, local authorities, and other statutory and philanthropic funders. MQI is guided by the values of dignity, respect, compassion, and inclusion in all of its work. 1.3 Further information on MQI can be found at www.mqi.ie. 1.4 MQI reserves the right to update or alter any information contained in this RFT at any time. 2. ETENDERS 2.1 MQI is utilising an electronic tendering system to manage this tender competition and communicate with Tenderers. Accordingly, there will be no hard copy documents issued to Tenderers and all communications with MQI, including the submission of Tenders, will be conducted solely via the eTenders website at www.etenders.gov.ie. 3. This RFI extends to the U.S. and allied nation maritime industrial base with vessel designs that pertain to existing or production-ready oceanographic capable vessels which satisfy or closely satisfy the below preliminary capability and operating profile parameters necessary to accomplish the T-AGS(X) missions. *Represent a five-year average which includes required maintenance periods Additionally, PMS 325 would like to gain insight into recently proven execution and build strategies as well as the current capability, capacity, and availability of domestic shipyards to support the delivery of an oceanographic-capable vessel. PROGRAM BACKGROUND The program seeks to recapitalize the existing oceanographic survey ship fleet. This fleet provides marine and hydrographic data collection to support preparation of maps, charts, books, geodetic products, and numerical and oceanographic prediction The Department of the Navy’s (DON) current oceanographic survey ship capabilities are provided by six PATHFINDER (T-AGS 60) Class ships. The PATHFINDER Class is approaching the end of its expected service life and recapitalization is needed to maintain the Navy’s required capability. REQUESTED

Overside Handling | Capable of statically handling, deploying, and recovering large mission packages over the side at loads up to 10,000 lbs, including a 50 ft core sampler. Mission Related Deck Equipment | A suite of cranes, winches, stern A-frame, and other deck gear required to permit loading and unloading the ship without assistance to support a variety of oceanographic operations at sea. The winch system will have a slack tensioning subsystem, and the tow winch system is located below decks to protect from the elements. Provision for the remote control of permanently installed mission-related winches from weather-protected enclosure(s) with maximum practicable visibility of the cable to the last overside block or sheave. Acquisition strategy – The Navy is considering alternative acquisition approaches and/or the use of a vessel construction manager or streamlined government quality assurance processes. Please share your perspective on the potential impacts associated with these approaches. Do you have suggestions for how PMS 325 could modify its acquisition approach to reduce costs, minimize risks, and/or expedite delivery schedule? Schedule – please provide a notional schedule to complete a production-ready design production duration for a fleet of up to eight vessels by hull (e.g., a Gantt chart). Cost Estimate – please provide a rough order of magnitude cost estimate for design (parent craft design modification, if proposed, or production-ready design). Please provide a separate rough order of magnitude cost estimate for production of up to eight vessels. Please include relevant assumptions (e.g., inflation, labor rates). Note: This ROM is non-binding and for planning purposes only. Discreet and Covert Operations – please provide design examples for completing discreet and covert operations for this vessel. Specifically, the Navy is investigating if a moonpool is required for these operations or if there is an alternative method. The Navy would also like to know how this method would impact the design features and cost. certifications_partner.text: ships are used by Naval Oceanographic Office (NAVOCEANO) to collect data that enables timely, accurate, and actional environmental information. This RFI seeks available oceanographic designs from the U.S. and allied nation maritime industrial bases, including an understanding of the level of maturity of each design. This RFI also requests information regarding industry capability to produce hydrographic and bathymetric-capable vessels from within the U.S. maritime industrial base. The ships will be designed and built to commercial regulatory body requirements (e.g. American Bureau of Shipping Marine Vessel Rules), obtain a U.S. Coast Guard Certificate of Inspection, and comply with other regulatory body regulations, such as International Marine Pollution Regulations and Safety of Life at Sea, as appropriate. T-AGS(X) will have a civilian mariner crew and embarked NAVOCEANO surveyors. This RFI extends to the U.S. and allied nation maritime industrial base with vessel designs that pertain to existing or production-ready oceanographic capable vessels which satisfy or closely satisfy the below preliminary capability and operating profile parameters necessary to accomplish the T-AGS(X) missions. *Represent a five-year average which includes required maintenance periods Additionally, PMS 325 w

in any future solicitation, if one is issued. Parameter | Requirement Mission Requirements | Ability to launch, operate, and recover mission equipment while holding position, with a sustained wind speed of 27 knots and a current speed at best heading in NATO Sea State (SS) 5. Operating Environment | Classed for unrestricted service. Engineered to operate navigable oceans including subarctic waters beginning 50°N. Hydrographic surveys conducted in depths less than 200 meters. Speed | Minimum 15 knots in all headings in seas, up to the top of NATO SS4. 10 knots on best heading, up to the top of NATO SS5. Dynamic Positioning | ABS DP-2 certification or equivalent. Maintain position and any heading within 33-ft radius with minimum current of 2 knots, 27-knot sustained wind, and seas up to NATO SS5. Maintain trackline within plus or minus 10 ft at 0.5 to 12 knots with a minimum 5,000 lb towing force. Endurance | Capable of 12,000 nautical miles at 12 knots plus 29 days at 3 knots, with a 10% fuel reserve. Draft | Less than 30 feet at full load. Acoustic Characteristics | Reduction of hull-induced flow noise and bubble sweep down. All installed sonars operate at full performance at up to 12 knots in NATO SS4. Accommodate minimum 100kW electrical generator for up to 6 hours. Mee

deliverables_scope.text: Ships (T-AGS(X)) that perform acoustical, biological, physical and geophysical surveys. T-AGS ships are used by Naval Oceanographic Office (NAVOCEANO) to collect data that enables timely, accurate, and actional environmental information. This RFI seeks available oceanographic designs from the U.S. and allied nation maritime industrial bases, including an understanding of the level of maturity of each design. This RFI also requests information regarding industry capability to produce hydrographic and bathymetric-capable vessels from within the U.S. maritime industrial base. The ships will be designed and built to commercial regulatory body requirements (e.g. American Bureau of Shipping Marine Vessel Rules), obtain a U.S. Coast Guard Certificate of Inspection, and comply with other regulatory body regulations, such as International Marine Pollution Regulations and Safety of Life at Sea, as appropriate. T-AGS(X) will have a civilian mariner crew and embarked NAVOCEANO surveyors. This RFI extends to the U.S. and allied nation maritime industrial base with vessel designs that pertain to existing or production-ready oceanographic capable vessels which satisfy or closely satisfy the below preliminary capability and operating profile parameters necessary to accomplish the T-AGS(X) missions. *Rep

Responses to this notice are not offers and will not be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract or agreement. The Government will not be obligated to pursue any particular acquisition alternative because of this RFI. Responses to the RFI will not be returned. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future solicitation, if one is issued. PROGRAM BACKGROUND The program seeks to recapitalize the existing oceanographic survey ship fleet. This fleet provides marine and hydrographic data collection to support preparation of maps, charts, books, geodetic products, and numerical and oceanographic prediction The Department of the Navy’s (DON) current oceanographic survey ship capabilities are provided by six PATHFINDER (T-AGS 60) Class ships. The PATHFINDER Class is approaching the end of its expected service life and recapitalization is needed to maintain the Navy’s required capability. REQUESTED

Overside Handling | Capable of statically handling, deploying, and recovering large mission packages over the side at loads up to 10,000 lbs, including a 50 ft core sampler. Mission Related Deck Equipment | A suite of cranes, winches, stern A-frame, and other deck gear required to permit loading and unloading the ship without assistance to support a variety of oceanographic operations at sea. The winch system will have a slack tensioning subsystem, and the tow winch system is located below decks to protect from the elements. Provision for the remote control of permanently installed mission-related winches from weather-protected enclosure(s) with maximum practicable visibility of the cable to the last overside block or sheave.
